entry.title: Fix example in `String#replaceAll` to show advantage of `RegExp.escape` vs string arg
entry.content:
Description

Fix example in String#replaceAll to show potential advantage of RegExp.escape over passing a string argument directly.

Motivation

Current wording "it is better to just use replaceAll() and pass the string" isn't necessarily correct, e.g. you may want to only match at word boundaries (I've used non-Unicode-aware \b boundaries in the example to avoid overcomplicating).

entry.title: fix(ff-relnote-experimental): Reorder the updates in reverse chronological order
entry.content:
Description

This PR reorders the entries in each technology section in the descending order by the Nightly version they were introduced in. This is already the order in the HTML DOM API section.

I've also removed some H4s because the parent H3s were sufficient and the prose contains other details:

  • "Primary payment handling" under Payment Request API
  • "ScreenOrientation.lock()" under Screen Orientation API
  • "WebVR API (Disabled)" under WebVR API

Updated the heading "Reporting API support for CSP Violations" to "Reporting API" for consistency with other headings in the API section.

Motivation

To allow developers to view the latest changes quickly without having to scroll through older updates.

entry.title: fix(js-code-style-guide): Make H3s parallel
entry.content:
Description

Currently, there is a mix of gerund and imperative language in H3 section headings in the JS code style guide.

This PR edits the H3 headings to follow a consistent, imperative tone, which helps to make the headings more action-oriented and explicit. This also helps to directly convey a recommendation via the headings.

  • Gerund-based headings (e.g., "Using modern JavaScript features") have been updated to imperative form ("Use modern JavaScript features when supported").
  • Passive headings (e.g., "Function declarations") have been updated to more actionable, imperative form ("Use function declarations to define functions").

Motivation

To ensure consistency in heading style and make the content more quickly scanable for best practices.

entry.title: Fix the "Exceptions" section of the VideoEncoder.encode() page

Description

The "Exceptions" section of the page for the new Web Codecs' API's VideoEncoder's encode() method (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/VideoEncoder/encode) is incorrect, specifically the description for DataError. entry.title: Add info about calling `remove()` on nodes that have no parent node
entry.content:
Description

Add info about calling remove() on nodes that have no parent node.

Also tightened up wording:

  • Element.remove doesn't always "remove the element from the DOM" (e.g. if the parent is already detached from the DOM)
  • CharacterData.remove doesn't "remove the text contained in the node", rather it removes the text node it from its parent, without altering its internal text data.

Motivation

Currently this info is missing.

Additional details

https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-childnode-remove

  1. If this’s parent is null, then return.
  2. Remove this.

entry.title: Fixing confusion around id versus name
entry.content:
Description

Clarifying the roles of id (aka "username") vs name (aka "display name") in this credential type, aligning them to typical expectations for username/password credentials.

Motivation

The existing documentation (and sample code) implies confusing/mixed things about the roles of id versus name in the creation and storage of this credential type. Some parts of this page were accurate (to spec) but other places implied an opposite relationship that contradicts the spec (and browser behavior).

I misunderstood after reading this page, and only figured it out after live testing -- including actually using navigator.credentials.store() to prompt to store the credential in the browser -- and reading the specification.

So I want to fix the page so other's aren't misled like I was. :)

Additional details

n/a

entry.title: docs(css): clarify that align-items: stretch also shrinks overflowing…
entry.content:
… items (#39491)

Description

Clarified the documentation for align-items: stretch to note that in addition to enlarging smaller items, it will also shrink overflowing items to fit the alignment container, respecting their width and height limits.

Motivation

This update addresses user confusion about the behavior of align-items: stretch when flex or grid items overflow the alignment container. It helps readers understand that the property will both enlarge and shrink items as needed, which aligns with expected behavior and resolves ambiguity in the docs.

Additional details

No code changes—only a documentation clarification. See discussion in issue #39491.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #39491

entry.title: Update Express tutorial to v5
entry.content:
This updates the Express Tutorial to v5

I wrote some tests in mdn/express-locallibrary-tutorial#327, then updated Express to v5 along with all dependencies - everything passed. Then ran all the code mods (npx @expressjs/codemod upgrade) suggested in the migration guide - nothing was changed. So I don't think I was using anything impacted by a changed or removed API.

What I do need to do though is remove my code to do async error handling in routes, since that is now handled automatically. I also want to update the structure of where mongoose is added to match the tests. The way it was done in the app.js means that tests can't work (because you can't have multiple connections, and if you do this in the app there is already a connection by the time you get to the test runner).

Actions:

  • Fix up all links from 4x to 5x
  • Fix up the mongoose instructions to set up the tests in the bin/www file.
  • Fix up later instructions that update the DB url so that they point to www.
  • Fix up environment instructions to match current LTS versions of node etc.
  • Fix up all dependencies.
  • Remove v4 patch for hacking async error handling
  • Work through and tidy up docs.
  • https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Extensions/Server-side/Express_Nodejs/routes#route_paths - I think this changed. Check in path route matching syntax in https://expressjs.com/en/guide/migrating-5.html#res.send.status

Fixes #38922
